assessment.nobel_worthiness: Their work transformed understanding of how technological change and trade shocks reshape local labour demand, employment and inequality.
assessment.attribution: Autor, Dorn and Hanson form a coherent core for distinct but closely connected evidence on task change and import competition.
assessment.maturity: The research has accumulated extensive evidence and remains central to policy and historical accounts of structural change.
uncertainties: The relative boundaries between technological and trade mechanisms remain contested.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: This research made management practices and organizational capital measurable economic explanations for persistent productivity differences.
assessment.attribution: Bloom and Van Reenen are central originators, with Sadun an important contributor to the organizational and empirical program.
assessment.maturity: The findings have been replicated across settings and have influenced research on firms, productivity and development.
uncertainties: Causal interpretation of management measures and their portability across institutional settings remain active questions.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Population administrative-data research on mobility changed both the measurement of opportunity and the study of place-based inequality.
assessment.attribution: Chetty, Hendren and Friedman represent a readily attributable core of the linked mobility research program.
assessment.maturity: The methods and results have produced a major durable literature and broad public relevance.
uncertainties: Some policy implications depend on extrapolation from observed geographic and cohort variation.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Their long-run comparative evidence put recurrent financial crises, sovereign debt and default at the center of macroeconomic historical analysis.
assessment.attribution: Reinhart and Rogoff are the clearly identifiable joint architects of this synthesis.
assessment.maturity: The agenda has had enduring influence on scholarship and crisis-policy debate.
uncertainties: Some headline empirical claims and data treatment have been debated, requiring careful separation of the broader contribution from particular estimates.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Their work supplied foundational economic frameworks for exhaustible resources, natural capital and the valuation of biodiversity.
assessment.attribution: Dasgupta and Heal have a strong, historically established claim to the core theoretical contribution.
assessment.maturity: The work is long-standing and increasingly consequential as environmental constraints enter economic measurement and policy.
uncertainties: Practical valuation of biodiversity and inclusive wealth necessarily depends on difficult measurement choices.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: This program fundamentally expanded the empirical study of top incomes, wealth concentration and hidden wealth over the long run.
assessment.attribution: Piketty and Saez are central to the distributional-data agenda, while Zucman is central to its offshore-wealth extension.
assessment.maturity: The work has generated large international data infrastructure and a sustained scholarly literature.
uncertainties: Distributional series and wealth capitalization methods entail consequential assumptions and continuing revisions.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Firm heterogeneity and selection became a foundational framework for explaining trade patterns, productivity and unequal gains from globalization.
assessment.attribution: Melitz provides the decisive foundational model; Helpman and Redding made major complementary theoretical and empirical contributions.
assessment.maturity: The framework is deeply integrated into modern trade research and has extensive empirical support.
uncertainties: The appropriate division of credit among the broader heterogeneous-firms literature is difficult.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Their political-economy research clarified how political institutions, state capacity and fiscal choices jointly shape long-run development.
assessment.attribution: Besley, Persson and Tabellini are leading and complementary contributors to a coherent institutional political-economy agenda.
assessment.maturity: The contribution has developed over decades and connects formal theory with influential empirical work.
uncertainties: Institutional causality is difficult to isolate, and the work spans several partially distinct research programs.
